thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGER — auth-proxy: unexpected auth 401 surge from multiple tenants (rate ~1.2k reqs/s). Suspicious log-forwarder activity flagged (indexer-shipper), possible token fragments in external uploads. Alert -> https://grafana.internal/r/alert/9981

Nina O: ack — i'm oncall. grabbing runbook + checking customer impact dashboards. who can pause the forwarder?

Tim L: i can take lead. looking at traces now, see flooding from ~40 unique IPs across regions. will pause log-forwarder in infra namespace and snapshot current logs.

Raj P: pausing now (infra). command i ran: `kubectl scale deploy/log-forwarder -n infra --replicas=0` — scaling to 0, verifying pods terminate. :white_check_mark:

Amanda S: sec here — initial ask: rotate the service account keys used by indexer-shipper, and temporarily block external S3 uploads from that job. recommend 30m window for key rotation + verification before re-enabling. also collect a sample of the forwarded artifacts (preserve for forensics).

Tim L: noted. starting key rotation: creating new service key, swapping creds in staging first. snippet: `aws iam create-access-key --user-name forwarder-svc` then update secret in k8s: `kubectl create secret generic forwarder-creds -n infra --from-literal=AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...`

sec-ops-bot: correlated anomalies: 3 tenant IDs show repeated 401->200 cycles and then large multipart uploads to external S3 endpoints. TTL for affected tokens looks short (minutes) — likely opportunistic scraping not long-term exfil. affected_tenants: tenant-phi-12, tenant-ecom-7, tenant-dev-3.

Nina O: customer impact check — are any production customers actively disrupted (401s)?

Tim L: customer logs: tenant-ecom-7 saw increased 401s around 10:02 UTC, many retries from our SDKs. but no large downstream errors (no successful data exfil confirmed yet).

Amanda S: legal/priv policy — collect preserved artifacts and open a low-likelihood data exposure ticket. we should plan rotation of the forwarder keys + revoke old keys immediately. escalation if we find PII in artifacts.

Raj P: egress isolation applied: added deny rule for log-forwarder service account to external S3 buckets in network policy. rollback plan ready if we need to re-enable.

Tim L: old keys revoked, new keys live in infra secrets, and k8s restarted forwarder as read-only (no upload path) to validate behavior. running smoke tests now.

Nina O: plan for comms: wait until we confirm artifacts snapshot and confirm no PII. if none, we send a proactive note to the three tenants explaining brief auth instability and mitigation steps. Amanda — can you prep the draft?

Amanda S: on it. draft will include timeline, mitigations taken (paused forwarder, rotated keys, isolated egress), ask to contact security if they notice anything. will loop legal for signoff.

Tim L: smoke tests good (auth flows normal, no outbound uploads). keeping forwarder disabled for 20 more mins while we finish checks.

Nina O: summary/actions: 1) Raj — egress isolate (done). 2) Tim — rotate creds + revoke old (done). 3) Amanda — artifacts preserved + draft customer comms (in progress). 4) Nina — coordinate follow-up & post-incident doc. moving this to active incident channel. :thumbsup:

sec-ops-bot: incident ticket created -> INC-2026-0427, severity: P2, initial owner: Nina O.

Nina O: thanks everyone — keep updates here. if we find sensitive data in artifacts we escalate to PagerDuty high and notify customers plus legal immediately.

Tim L: will post final verification in 15m and then we can discuss re-enabling the forwarder with stricter ACLs and shorter key TTL.

Amanda S: note for follow-up: add automated detection for token-fragments in uploads and require server-side encryption + tenant allowlist for forwarder jobs.

Nina O: copy. closing this thread for now to incident channel. reopen if anything changes. :lock:
